interest: Kate Smith's broadcast drew American tutor applications for the Crown Prince; a 1949 memo records Empress Nagako's education plan.
overview: This decimal file (894.0011) from the U.S. State Department records covers political affairs and sovereign family matters of Japan between July 1946 and February 1949, focusing specifically on the education of Crown Prince Akihito during the Allied occupation. The earlier portion (July 1946) concerns an unsolicited application from an American teacher, Helen Irvine Kennedy, who sought the position of tutor to the young Crown Prince after hearing a broadcast by radio personality Kate Smith; her letters to the Japanese Ambassador and Emperor Hirohito were redirected through the State Department to Dr. George D. Stoddard, head of the U.S. Education Mission to Japan. The later document (February 1949) is a confidential policy memorandum discussing an informal initiative by Empress Nagako to send the fifteen-year-old Crown Prince to preparatory school in the United States and university in England. The memorandum outlines contrasting views among General Douglas MacArthur, Political Adviser William J. Sebald, and Far Eastern Affairs Director W. Walton Butterworth regarding the timing, suitability, and political implications of Western boarding school education versus higher education abroad for the heir to the Chrysanthemum Throne.
